claim: Almost all the filtered blood glucose is reabsorbed by the kidneys.
source: Almost all the filtered blood glucose is reabsorbed by the kidneys.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and introduction without specific experimental data or citations in this manuscript.

claim: Loss of glucose in urine (glycosuria) is offset by an increase in endogenous glucose production to maintain normal energy supply in the body.
source: Loss of glucose in urine (glycosuria) is offset by an increase in endogenous glucose production to maintain normal energy supply in the body.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the abstract, supported by the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Elevated glycosuria activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Using renal Slc2a2 (also known as Glut2) knockout mice, we demonstrate that elevated glycosuria activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, which in turn drives endogenous glucose production.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing increased HPA axis markers (Crh, ACTH, corticosterone) in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice as shown in Figure 2.

claim: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis drives endogenous glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria.
source: Using renal Slc2a2 (also known as Glut2) knockout mice, we demonstrate that elevated glycosuria activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, which in turn drives endogenous glucose production.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between HPA axis activation and increased glucose production in the knockout mice, and the reversal of both phenotypes with afferent renal denervation.

claim: Selective afferent renal denervation attenuates the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: This phenotype was attenuated by selective afferent renal denervation, indicating the involvement of the afferent nerves in promoting the compensatory increase in glucose production.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing decreased blood glucose levels and restored HPA axis markers after afferent renal denervation as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Afferent renal nerves are involved in promoting the compensatory increase in glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria.
source: This phenotype was attenuated by selective afferent renal denervation, indicating the involvement of the afferent nerves in promoting the compensatory increase in glucose production.
evidence: This is inferred from the attenuation of the compensatory glucose production phenotype following afferent renal denervation.

claim: Acute phase proteins were the top candidates which were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 KO mice.
source: In addition, through plasma proteomics analyses we observed that acute phase proteins - which are usually involved in the body's defense mechanisms against a threat – were the top candidates which were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 KO mice.
evidence: This is supported by the 2D-DIGE and proteomic analyses data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Acute phase proteins are usually involved in the body's defense mechanisms against a threat.
source: In addition, through plasma proteomics analyses we observed that acute phase proteins - which are usually involved in the body's defense mechanisms against a threat – were the top candidates which were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 KO mice.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the function of acute phase proteins.

claim: Loss of glucose in urine is sensed as a biological threat in mice.
source: Overall, afferent renal nerves contribute to promoting endogenous glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria and loss of glucose in urine is sensed as a biological threat in mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the activation of defense mechanisms including HPA axis and acute phase proteins in response to glycosuria.

claim: The renal threshold for glucose reabsorption in humans is 180 mg/dl.
source: The renal threshold for glucose reabsorption in humans is 180 mg/dl and in rodents is about 400 mg/dl (Noonan and Banks, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Noonan and Banks, 2000.

claim: The renal threshold for glucose reabsorption in rodents is about 400 mg/dl.
source: The renal threshold for glucose reabsorption in humans is 180 mg/dl and in rodents is about 400 mg/dl (Noonan and Banks, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Noonan and Banks, 2000.

claim: Genetic loss of glucose transporters like GLUT2 can cause glucose to be excreted in the urine.
source: In conditions such as overt hyperglycemia (beyond the renal glucose threshold), genetic loss of glucose transporters like GLUT2 (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2021; de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022; Sakamoto et al., 2000) or SGLT2 (Kleta et al., 2004), and/or renal dysfunction, glucose is excreted in the urine.
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2021; de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022; Sakamoto et al., 2000.

claim: Genetic loss of SGLT2 can cause glucose to be excreted in the urine.
source: In conditions such as overt hyperglycemia (beyond the renal glucose threshold), genetic loss of glucose transporters like GLUT2 (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2021; de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022; Sakamoto et al., 2000) or SGLT2 (Kleta et al., 2004), and/or renal dysfunction, glucose is excreted in the urine.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kleta et al., 2004.

claim: Enhancing glycosuria through SGLT2 inhibition is used to reduce blood glucose levels in humans with diabetes.
source: Enhancing glycosuria, through SGLT2 inhibition (Rossetti et al., 1987; Oku et al., 1999; Han et al., 2008), is now used to reduce blood glucose levels in humans with diabetes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rossetti et al., 1987; Oku et al., 1999; Han et al., 2008.

claim: The glucose loss from SGLT2 inhibition is offset by a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production, compromising the efficacy of this strategy in the treatment of diabetes.
source: However, the glucose loss is offset by a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production, consequently compromising the efficacy of this strategy in the treatment of diabetes (Solis-Herrera et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Solis-Herrera et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice show massive glycosuria.
source: We recently produced renal Slc2a2 (also known as Glut2) knockout mice (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022), which show massive glycosuria and are protected from diabetes and diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022).

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice are protected from diabetes.
source: We recently produced renal Slc2a2 (also known as Glut2) knockout mice (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022), which show massive glycosuria and are protected from diabetes and diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022).

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice are protected from diet-induced obesity.
source: We recently produced renal Slc2a2 (also known as Glut2) knockout mice (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022), which show massive glycosuria and are protected from diabetes and diet-induced obesity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022).

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice maintain normal fasting blood glucose levels despite the loss of glucose in the urine.
source: Despite the loss of glucose in the urine, renal Slc2a2 knockout mice maintain normal fasting blood glucose levels.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the authors' previous work and is consistent with the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There is a fundamental mechanism involved in sensing glucose loss and triggering a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production in rodents and humans.
source: Collectively, these observations indicate the presence of a fundamental mechanism involved in sensing glucose loss and triggering a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production in rodents and humans.
evidence: This is inferred from the observations in both renal Slc2a2 knockout mice and humans treated with SGLT2 inhibitors.

claim: The mechanism of compensatory glucose production in response to glycosuria is aligned with established survival strategies that reduce utilization and increase the production of glucose during a flight or fight response against a threat.
source: This mechanism is also aligned with the established survival strategies that reduce utilization and increase the production of glucose (energy) during a flight or fight response against a threat (Surwit et al., 1992; Marik and Bellomo, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Surwit et al., 1992; Marik and Bellomo, 2013.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice exhibit normal fasting blood glucose levels despite massive glycosuria.
source: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice exhibit normal fasting blood glucose levels despite massive glycosuria (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022.

claim: Normal fasting blood glucose levels in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice despite massive glycosuria suggests a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production.
source: This observation suggests a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production, similar to that observed in humans following SGLT2 inhibition (Solis-Herrera et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012; Daniele et al., 2020).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation and supported by citations to similar findings in humans (Solis-Herrera et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012; Daniele et al., 2020).

claim: Both liver and kidney tissues contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We observed that both tissues contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 1a–c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data measuring hepatic and renal glucose production shown in Figure 1a-c.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have decreased hepatic glucose 6-phosphate.
source: This was accompanied by a decrease in hepatic glucose 6-phosphate, glucose 1-phosphate, and fructose 6-phosphate (Figure 1d–f), suggesting a decline in glucose metabolism in favor of increasing glucose production.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have decreased hepatic glucose 1-phosphate.
source: This was accompanied by a decrease in hepatic glucose 6-phosphate, glucose 1-phosphate, and fructose 6-phosphate (Figure 1d–f), suggesting a decline in glucose metabolism in favor of increasing glucose production.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have decreased hepatic fructose 6-phosphate.
source: This was accompanied by a decrease in hepatic glucose 6-phosphate, glucose 1-phosphate, and fructose 6-phosphate (Figure 1d–f), suggesting a decline in glucose metabolism in favor of increasing glucose production.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The decrease in hepatic glucose 6-phosphate, glucose 1-phosphate, and fructose 6-phosphate in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice suggests a decline in glucose metabolism in favor of increasing glucose production.
source: This was accompanied by a decrease in hepatic glucose 6-phosphate, glucose 1-phosphate, and fructose 6-phosphate (Figure 1d–f), suggesting a decline in glucose metabolism in favor of increasing glucose production.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolite data showing decreased levels of glycolytic intermediates.

claim: The HPA axis is a major stress response system involved in enhancing glucose production.
source: The HPA axis is a major stress response system involved in enhancing glucose production.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the HPA axis.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have increased plasma corticosterone.
source: Therefore, we measured plasma corticosterone and adrenocorticotropin hormone coupled with gene expression of hypothalamic corticotropic releasing hormone (Crh). We observed an increase in all these factors (Figure 2) that comprise the HPA axis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have increased plasma adrenocorticotropin hormone.
source: Therefore, we measured plasma corticosterone and adrenocorticotropin hormone coupled with gene expression of hypothalamic corticotropic releasing hormone (Crh). We observed an increase in all these factors (Figure 2) that comprise the HPA axis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice have increased expression of hypothalamic corticotropic releasing hormone (Crh).
source: Therefore, we measured plasma corticosterone and adrenocorticotropin hormone coupled with gene expression of hypothalamic corticotropic releasing hormone (Crh). We observed an increase in all these factors (Figure 2) that comprise the HPA axis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a and 2b.

claim: The increase in HPA axis factors suggests that the HPA axis may contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: These findings suggest that the HPA axis may contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between HPA axis activation and increased glucose production.

claim: Capsaicin was used to selectively suppress afferent renal nerve activity in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: To determine the role of afferent renal nerves in triggering a compensatory glucose production in response to glycosuria, we used capsaicin to selectively suppress afferent renal nerve activity in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is stated as the experimental method used.

claim: Afferent denervation was confirmed by measuring renal pelvic CGRP at the end of the study.
source: Afferent denervation was confirmed by measuring renal pelvic CGRP (pg/mg protein) at the end of this study (Sham: 86.3±6.4 (control mice), 93.7±8.2 (renal Slc2a2 knockout mice); Capsaicin: 4.7±0.06 (control mice), 6.4±0.7 (renal Slc2a2 knockout mice), using ELISA kit, Cayman Chemical, 589001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data measuring CGRP levels.

claim: Fasting blood glucose levels were about 50% decreased in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their control littermates after afferent renal denervation.
source: We observed that fasting and fed (random) blood glucose levels were about 50% decreased in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their control littermates (Figure 3a and b) after the afferent renal denervation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: Fed (random) blood glucose levels were about 50% decreased in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their control littermates after afferent renal denervation.
source: We observed that fasting and fed (random) blood glucose levels were about 50% decreased in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their control littermates (Figure 3a and b) after the afferent renal denervation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: Afferent renal denervation reversed the activation of the HPA axis in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: In addition, the denervation reversed the activation of the HPA axis in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 3c and d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c and 3d.

claim: Fasting plasma insulin levels were not changed after afferent renal denervation.
source: Fasting plasma insulin levels were not changed (Figure 3e) after the denervation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Renal nerves partly contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: These observations suggest that renal nerves partly contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the partial reversal of the glucose production phenotype following afferent renal denervation.

claim: The denervation procedure did not influence baseline blood glucose levels in the control mice.
source: It is important to note that the denervation procedure did not influence baseline blood glucose levels (Figure 3a and b) or plasma insulin levels (Figure 3e) in the control mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: The denervation procedure did not influence plasma insulin levels in the control mice.
source: It is important to note that the denervation procedure did not influence baseline blood glucose levels (Figure 3a and b) or plasma insulin levels (Figure 3e) in the control mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The denervation procedure did not change baseline food intake in control mice.
source: Similarly, the procedure did not change baseline food intake or body weight in these mice (food intake: 3.7±0.4 vs 4±0.3 g/day; body weight: 26.8±3.6 vs 27.7±5.3 g, sham vs afferent renal denervation).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing food intake between sham and denervated control mice.

claim: The denervation procedure did not change baseline body weight in control mice.
source: Similarly, the procedure did not change baseline food intake or body weight in these mice (food intake: 3.7±0.4 vs 4±0.3 g/day; body weight: 26.8±3.6 vs 27.7±5.3 g, sham vs afferent renal denervation).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing body weight between sham and denervated control mice.

claim: There was no change in total renal nerve activity in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Although the afferent renal denervation procedure attenuated the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice, unexpectedly there was no change in their total or afferent renal nerve activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a and b.

claim: There was no change in afferent renal nerve activity in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Although the afferent renal denervation procedure attenuated the compensatory increase in glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice, unexpectedly there was no change in their total or afferent renal nerve activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a and b.

claim: Neuroendocrine mechanisms independent of changes in renal nerve activity may be involved in increasing glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: These findings suggest that neuroendocrine mechanisms independent of changes in renal nerve activity may be involved in increasing glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that glucose production was affected despite no change in renal nerve activity.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar heart rate to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar weights of brown adipose tissue to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar weights of white adipose tissue to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1f-h.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar kidney weight to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1i.

claim: Renal Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar liver weight to control mice.
source: In addition, the Slc2a2 knockout mice had similar blood pressure, heart rate coupled with similar weights of brown and white adipose tissue, kidney, and liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c–j).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1j.

claim: Afferent renal nerves partly contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production to make up for glucose loss in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Altogether, the results indicate that afferent renal nerves partly contribute to the compensatory increase in glucose production to make up for glucose loss in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the partial reversal of the glucose production phenotype following afferent renal denervation.

claim: Renal nerves may be involved in mediating a compensatory increase in glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria by SGLT2 inhibition in humans.
source: These findings support the data from humans (Daniele et al., 2020) that renal nerves may be involved in mediating a compensatory increase in glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria by SGLT2 inhibition.
evidence: This is inferred from the mouse data and supported by a citation to human data (Daniele et al., 2020).

claim: Renal nerves are significant in regulating systemic glucose homeostasis in rodents.
source: In addition, the findings are aligned with the previous studies in rodents demonstrating the significance of renal nerves in regulating systemic glucose homeostasis (Chhabra et al., 2017; Jiman et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chhabra et al., 2017; Jiman et al., 2018.

claim: Mannose-binding lectin was upregulated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We observed that acute-phase proteins like mannose-binding lectin, albumin, haptoglobin, and ferritin were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Albumin levels were altered in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We observed that acute-phase proteins like mannose-binding lectin, albumin, haptoglobin, and ferritin were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Haptoglobin levels were altered in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We observed that acute-phase proteins like mannose-binding lectin, albumin, haptoglobin, and ferritin were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Ferritin levels were altered in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We observed that acute-phase proteins like mannose-binding lectin, albumin, haptoglobin, and ferritin were either upregulated or downregulated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Levels of acute phase proteins are usually changed in response to threat, infection, and/or injury to activate the body's defense systems.
source: Usually, levels of these proteins are changed in response to threat, infection, and/or injury to activate the body's defense systems (Gabay and Kushner, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gabay and Kushner, 1999.

claim: Major urinary proteins like MUP18 were elevated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Similarly, major urinary proteins (MUP) like MUP18, which belong to the lipocalin protein family, were elevated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Major urinary proteins belong to the lipocalin protein family.
source: Similarly, major urinary proteins (MUP) like MUP18, which belong to the lipocalin protein family, were elevated in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about MUPs.

claim: Major urinary proteins are involved in regulating inter-organ chemical signaling, pheromonal communication, and energy metabolism.
source: These proteins are involved in regulating inter-organ chemical signaling, pheromonal communication, and energy metabolism (Zhou and Rui, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhou and Rui, 2010.

claim: Secreted glutathione peroxidase 3 (Gpx3) was the most downregulated protein in plasma in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: We also observed that secreted glutathione peroxidase 3 (Gpx3) was the most downregulated protein in plasma in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (Figure 4 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by plasma proteomics data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Gpx3 is predominantly expressed in the kidneys.
source: Gpx3 is predominantly expressed in the kidneys and is an anti-oxidant (Whitin et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Whitin et al., 2002.

claim: Gpx3 is an anti-oxidant.
source: Gpx3 is predominantly expressed in the kidneys and is an anti-oxidant (Whitin et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Whitin et al., 2002.

claim: Renal Gpx3 gene expression was about 50% lower in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their littermate controls.
source: Renal Gpx3 gene expression was about 50% lower (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a) in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice compared to their littermate controls.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Renal Mup18 gene expression was higher in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice relative to their controls.
source: Moreover, renal - but not hepatic - Mup18 gene expression was higher (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b and c) in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice relative to their controls, suggesting that the kidneys were responsible for increasing plasma MUP18 in the knockout mice.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Hepatic Mup18 gene expression was not different in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice relative to their controls.
source: Moreover, renal - but not hepatic - Mup18 gene expression was higher (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b and c) in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice relative to their controls, suggesting that the kidneys were responsible for increasing plasma MUP18 in the knockout mice.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The kidneys were responsible for increasing plasma MUP18 in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Moreover, renal - but not hepatic - Mup18 gene expression was higher (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b and c) in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice relative to their controls, suggesting that the kidneys were responsible for increasing plasma MUP18 in the knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that renal but not hepatic Mup18 expression was increased.

claim: Multiple pathways including local (renal) stress and general (HPA axis) stress response combined with the acute phase proteins compensate for glucose loss in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that multiple pathways - including local (renal) stress and general (HPA axis) stress response combined with the acute phase proteins - compensate for glucose loss and defend against a perceived biological threat in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of HPA axis activation and acute phase protein changes.

claim: Multiple pathways defend against a perceived biological threat in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that multiple pathways - including local (renal) stress and general (HPA axis) stress response combined with the acute phase proteins - compensate for glucose loss and defend against a perceived biological threat in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of HPA axis activation and acute phase protein changes.

claim: Higher urine volume (polyuria) observed in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice may contribute to an increase in glucose production to some extent.
source: Higher urine volume (polyuria) observed in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice may contribute to an increase in glucose production to some extent, however, that contribution would likely be minor based on previous studies (Hall et al., 2020; Perry et al., 2019) about the role of diuretics (which increase urine volume) in glucose production.
evidence: This is speculated based on citations to Hall et al., 2020; Perry et al., 2019.

claim: The contribution of polyuria to increased glucose production would likely be minor based on previous studies about the role of diuretics in glucose production.
source: Higher urine volume (polyuria) observed in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice may contribute to an increase in glucose production to some extent, however, that contribution would likely be minor based on previous studies (Hall et al., 2020; Perry et al., 2019) about the role of diuretics (which increase urine volume) in glucose production.
evidence: This is inferred from citations to Hall et al., 2020; Perry et al., 2019.

claim: Afferent renal denervation may have attenuated only hepatic glucose production through the hypothalamus axis without affecting the compensatory increase in renal glucose production.
source: It is possible that afferent renal denervation in the present study attenuated only hepatic glucose production through the hypothalamus axis without affecting the compensatory increase in renal (which is the local site of denervation in this study) glucose production.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible explanation for the partial effect of denervation.

claim: If afferent renal denervation attenuated only hepatic glucose production, this would explain why the denervation did not completely block the compensatory glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
source: If validated, this would explain why the afferent denervation did not completely block the compensatory glucose production in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible explanation for the partial effect of denervation.

claim: Male and female renal Slc2a2 knockout mice did not show sex differences in the phenotype related to glucose homeostasis.
source: Although we didn't observe sex differences in the phenotype related to glucose homeostasis in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022), some of the responses to elevated glycosuria reported here may be different between male and female mice.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022.

claim: Some of the responses to elevated glycosuria may be different between male and female mice.
source: Although we didn't observe sex differences in the phenotype related to glucose homeostasis in renal Slc2a2 knockout mice (de Souza Cordeiro et al., 2022), some of the responses to elevated glycosuria reported here may be different between male and female mice.
evidence: This is speculated as a limitation of the study.

claim: A kidney-hypothalamus axis contributes to triggering a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria in mice.
source: In summary, we report that a kidney-hypothalamus axis contributes to triggering a compensatory increase in endogenous glucose production in response to elevated glycosuria in mice.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the experimental data showing HPA axis activation and the effect of afferent renal denervation.

claim: Glucose loss in urine appears to be sensed as a biological threat and activates the body's defense systems including some of the acute phase proteins.
source: Glucose loss in urine appears to be sensed as a biological threat and therefore activates the body's defense systems including some of the acute phase proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the activation of HPA axis and changes in acute phase proteins.

claim: These findings may explain why SGLT2 inhibitors do not achieve their full potential in lowering blood glucose levels during the treatment of diabetes mellitus.
source: These findings may explain why SGLT2 inhibitors do not achieve their full potential in lowering blood glucose levels during the treatment of diabetes mellitus.
evidence: This is speculated as a potential clinical implication of the findings.

claim: Capsaicin ablates afferent renal nerves without affecting the blood vessels or efferent renal nerves.
source: This procedure ablates afferent renal nerves without affecting the blood vessels or efferent renal nerves (Foss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foss et al., 2015.

claim: 73 metabolites were measured in the liver metabolomics analysis.
source: 73 metabolites were measured, out of which nine were significantly (p<0.05) different (1.5 fold-change thresholds, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the metabolomics data.

claim: Nine metabolites were significantly different between renal Slc2a2 knockout and control mice in the liver metabolomics analysis.
source: 73 metabolites were measured, out of which nine were significantly (p<0.05) different (1.5 fold-change thresholds, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the metabolomics data.
